style: STYLE: a heraldry-inspired emblem for a grim dark-fantasy medieval rulebook, drawn in black ink pen on pure white paper like a bold woodcut or a medieval armorial stamp. DETAIL LEVEL: halfway between a flat icon and a detailed engraving. The charge has a strong solid-black silhouette PLUS clear interior ink lines that describe its form and character (for example: the fuller and grip wrapping of a blade, the stones of a wall, the scales and teeth of a beast, the folds of cloth, the barbs of a feather), and at most a few bold, widely spaced parallel strokes on the shadowed side to suggest form. Every line is confident and of medium-to-bold weight; nothing thin, fine or crowded. Strictly black and white: every mark is solid black or untouched white. NO grey, no wash, no gradients, no soft shading, no fine or dense hatching, no cross-hatching, no stippling, no paper texture, no 3D render, no drop shadow. It must still read clearly when printed half an inch tall. Grim and weathered: the shield rim is chipped and dented, shown by its outline. Centred on a plain white background with a wide empty margin on every side. No text, letters, numbers, mottoes or watermarks. No mantling, crest, helm above the shield, supporters, crown, frame, scroll or scenery.
series: SERIES: one of fifteen chapter arms that must read as a matched set. Every shield is the same upright heater shield (flat top, straight sides curving to a point), seen straight on, with the same bold double rim (a thick black outer line, a white gap, a thinner black inner line), slightly chipped, and the same proportions. The field inside the rim is plain white. One central charge fills about two thirds of the shield, drawn with the same weight of line and the same amount of detail as every other shield in the set.

items.subject: The emblem of HERALDRY SKIRMISH: THE DYING LANDS. A battle-worn heater shield, broken: one jagged crack runs from the top edge down into the shield and through the castle, and a chunk has broken off the upper right corner, with two or three small fragments falling away. On the plain white field, a castle charge: a gatehouse of three crenellated towers, the middle one tallest, in solid black with white masonry joint lines suggesting stone courses, a white arched gate with a portcullis drawn in a few bold black bars, and narrow white arrow slits. Bold double black rim, dented and chipped. Noble, ancient and ruined: the arms of a fallen realm.

Charge: an abstract old map, shown as a simple torn sheet of parchment, slightly curled at the corners, drawn in bold outline. On it: a rough coastline of one landmass in solid black, a winding white road or river across it, three small triangular mountain peaks, and a small four-pointed compass star in one corner. Simple and symbolic, like a map icon, with no readable text.
items.superseded: round 5: the map was rejected; see 01A to 01D

items.subject: Charge: a withered oak tree eradicated (torn up by the roots), the classic heraldic tree, drawn BOLD for a small icon: a thick solid black gnarled trunk with one or two white bark lines and a hollow knot; five to seven heavy bare branches that fork only once or twice and end in a few thick twisted points (no fine twigs, no thin lines); below, five or six thick exposed roots spreading out and ending in torn tips. A strong, simple silhouette that stays readable half an inch tall. The dead tree of a dying world and of its long memory.

Charge: a raven perched on a broken crown. The raven is a large bold solid black silhouette in profile, wings folded, beak open, a few white feather lines on the wing and a white eye. Its talons grip a crown below that is plainly BROKEN: the circlet cracked clean through and split open, one of its points snapped off and lying tilted beside it. The crown is drawn simply, black with a white band and a few white jewel dots. The bird of memory perched on the ruin of the kings.
Charge: a closed ancient tome bound shut with an iron chain and a padlock, solid black leather cover with white corner bosses and a white clasp, the chain crossing it in bold links. Forbidden lore.

Charge: an unrolled parchment scroll, its ends rolled, with a heavy wax seal hanging from it on a cord, the seal broken in two; the scroll's face shows a few bold black lines that are not readable letters. The chronicle of a fallen realm.

Charge: a single old bone die in three-quarter view, white faces outlined in bold black, chipped corners, solid black pips (one, two and three on the visible faces), the shadowed face marked with a few bold parallel strokes.

Charge: an hourglass in a turned wooden frame with three posts, the frame solid black with white turning lines, the glass drawn as a bold outline, sand as a solid black heap below and a thin falling stream.

Charge: three arrows side by side, parallel and upright, all pointing straight downward (in heraldic terms, three arrows in pale points down), each with a solid black barbed head at the bottom and white-and-black fletching at the top. Bold and evenly spaced, filling the shield.

Charge: two DIFFERENT weapons crossed in saltire, points upward: a heavy bearded battle axe and a notched, battle-worn longsword. The axe head is solid black with a chipped white edge; the sword blade has nicks along its edges and a black fuller; worn grips with white wrapping lines. Brutal and grim: weapons of a long, losing war, scarred and heavy. No blood, no gore.
Charge: a tattered swallow-tailed war banner flying from a lance, the banner solid black with a white cross and white fold lines, its ends frayed into a few points, the lance with a leaf-shaped head.

Charge: a piece of medieval chest armour: a breastplate (cuirass) seen from the front, solid black with a white central ridge, a white rolled neck edge, a row of white rivet dots along the borders and a short skirt of overlapping plates (fauld) below; one or two dents in its outline.
Charge: a tall flame of three tongues rising from a footed iron brazier; the flame solid black with white inner flame lines, the brazier bowl solid black with white rivet dots and a white band.
items.superseded: round 4: both flame concepts rejected; see 08A to 08C

items.subject: Charge: an open right hand raised palm outward, solid black, with a single white open eye drawn in the centre of the palm and a few short bold rays around the fingertips: the mark of the sorcerer and the priest.
Charge: a gnarled wooden staff held upright, its head a clawed iron cage gripping a faceted crystal drawn in white with black facet lines, a few short bold rays bursting from the crystal.
Charge: a sigil of power: a solid black circle enclosing a white five-pointed star, ringed by a band of simple angular marks that are clearly not letters, with a few short bold rays outside the ring.

Charge: a horned wyvern's head in profile facing left, jaws open showing white fangs, solid black with white lines for scales along the neck, a white eye and brow ridge, the neck torn off in a jagged edge.
Charge: a ruined round-arched stone gateway, one side of the arch collapsed, drawn as solid black blocks separated by white mortar lines, with a few fallen blocks at its foot.
Charge: a medieval war pavilion with a peaked roof, solid black with white lines for the roof seams and a scalloped valance, a white open door flap, a small pennant flying from the pole.
Charge: a large iron key, upright, its bow at the top with a white quatrefoil opening, solid black with white lines for the collar rings on the shank and the notched wards at the bottom.
Charge: a hanging iron lantern with a ring and a pointed cap, solid black frame with white panes crossed by bold black bars, a small black flame inside with a white core.
Charge: an open book seen from above, solid black cover edges, white pages with a few bold black lines for text (no readable letters), a ribbon bookmark hanging below the spine.
Charge: a quill feather set diagonally into a round ink pot below it; the feather solid black with white barb lines along the vane, the ink pot solid black with a white rim line.

Redraw it as one crown broken cleanly into exactly TWO separate halves, with a clear gap of white between the halves. The left half sits under the raven's talons, which grip it; the right half lies just beside it, slightly tilted, as if it has fallen away. Both halves are plainly the two parts of the same crown: matching band, points and jewels, with jagged broken edges where they split. There must be no other fragments, shards, chips or loose pieces anywhere: only the two halves.

A single medieval silver penny seen straight on, as a bold flat icon: a hammered coin, slightly irregular and not perfectly round, with one small clipped notch in its edge. A bold beaded border runs just inside the rim. In the centre, the classic long-cross design: a voided cross (each arm drawn as a bold double line) reaching to the beaded border, with three solid black pellets clustered in each of the four quarters. The coin face is white, all lines and pellets solid black, with a bold black outer rim. Simple, strong and instantly readable as a coin when printed only a few millimetres wide, the size of a letter of text. No letters or legend around the edge, no face, no shading.
